title: Just 400 US Data Centers Use More Electricity Than Michigan
gist: A Harvard study in Nature Sustainability finds 403 US hyperscale data centers used as much electricity as Michigan in a year, mostly from fossil fuels, with data center emissions triple pre-AI-boom levels. The study likely understates the trend, because new campuses are far larger than its 40 MW average and 189 GW of behind-the-meter, often gas-fired, generation is planned. Federal tracking via EIA surveys may be coming.

insights.claim: A Harvard study in Nature Sustainability found that about 400 US hyperscale data centers used as much electricity as the state of Michigan in a single year, mostly generated from fossil fuels.
insights.speaker: Molly Taft
insights.so_what: Quantifies data-center load at a state-sized level; supports thesis for grid, gas and power-generation demand.

insights.claim: Data center emissions are three times higher than they were before the AI boom, according to the Harvard study.
insights.speaker: Molly Taft
insights.so_what: Rising emissions intensify regulatory and community pushback risk for AI infrastructure build-outs.
insights.locator: The study, published Monday in Nature Sustainability

insights.claim: The Harvard researchers built a dataset of 403 hyperscale data centers operational between May 2024 and April 2025 using industry research and satellite data, then modeled energy use and regional grid mixes to estimate per-facility emissions.
insights.speaker: Molly Taft
insights.so_what: Satellite-plus-modeling methods can pierce data-center opacity; useful alt-data approach for tracking capacity.

insights.claim: Data centers in Virginia, Oregon, Ohio and Iowa accounted for more than 50 percent of the energy use in the Harvard study, with Virginia home to Data Center Alley.
insights.speaker: Molly Taft
insights.so_what: Grid strain and utility opportunity are geographically concentrated; focus on utilities and grid operators in these states.
insights.locator: Not all regions were created equal

insights.claim: The average facility in the Harvard study is 40 megawatts, while developers are now building campuses of hundreds or thousands of megawatts, so the study may already understate data center power use.
insights.speaker: Molly Taft
insights.so_what: Forward power demand likely exceeds backward-looking estimates; bullish for generation and grid equipment.
insights.quote: Some of the massive campuses being proposed today are substantially larger than the typical facility in our dataset
insights.locator: While based on recent data, the study

insights.claim: As much as 189 gigawatts of behind-the-meter power generation is in the US pipeline earmarked for data centers, increasingly relying on inefficient natural gas turbines, a factor Jon Koomey calls a 'wild card' for measuring total data center power.
insights.speaker: Molly Taft
insights.so_what: Huge on-site gas buildout is a demand driver for gas turbines and natural gas, and a blind spot in grid statistics.
insights.locator: The study also does not look at developers

insights.claim: BloombergNEF estimates that if all behind-the-meter power plants in the US development queue are built, overall US emissions could rise by 10 percent.
insights.speaker: Molly Taft
insights.so_what: Material macro emissions impact raises odds of climate-policy or permitting backlash against on-site gas for AI.
insights.locator: The study also does not look at developers

insights.claim: Federal and state governments do not track data center electricity use separately from the power sector, and individual facilities' consumption is often treated as proprietary, so operators and utilities need not disclose it.
insights.speaker: Molly Taft
insights.so_what: Opacity hampers grid planning and investor estimates of AI power demand; disclosure mandates would be a market-moving data source.
insights.quote: Sometimes we know it, but sometimes it’s behind an NDA, and no one ever sees it.
insights.locator: Federal and state governments do not track

insights.claim: The Energy Information Agency completed three pilot surveys of data center power use across 10 states this year and is using them to design a potential voluntary survey of the sector.
insights.speaker: Molly Taft
insights.so_what: An EIA data center survey would create the first official dataset on AI power demand; watch for its launch.
